title: How many places can you tell apart?

data.source: Cramer (1946), Rao (1945), Wootters (1981). Checked on simulated draws from the worked circle of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md, seeded.

prediction: If the ruler sigma is the Cramer-Rao width 1/sqrt(n), it is the same everywhere on the circle, the count a/sigma is Wootters' number of distinguishable places, and the wider notes' product C times Omega is 1 at every large n, so it cannot mark a moment.
baseline: The Cramer-Rao bound (Rao 1945, Cramer 1946) and Wootters' statistical distance (1981).
why: The spread of the best estimate, in Fisher arc, was the Cramer-Rao value at every place tested, so a Cramer-Rao ruler gives CRR's count exactly the meaning Wootters gave it in 1981. The wider notes' "C times Omega = 1" is the bound itself: the product crept down towards 1 as looks were added (my tolerance at 50 and 100 looks was too tight and that miss is recorded) and then stayed there, so it is a limit and not an event. Phoenix records sigma only as an independently calibrated unit (BASE, and ASSUMPTION R1); it does not claim this reading, and the number of looks n is still a free choice.
